learningObjective: Reason about the relative energy costs of on-chip compute vs off-chip memory access and their implications for DNN accelerator design.
stem: Survey figures (Sze et al., cited widely from Horowitz's ISSCC 2014 numbers) place DRAM access energy roughly 2–3 orders of magnitude above an on-chip multiply-add. Which of the following implications are correct for accelerator/DNN energy analysis? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Reducing DRAM accesses (via on-chip data reuse, tiling, buffer sharing) is often the largest lever for energy efficiency in DNN inference, even when compute FLOPs stay constant.
Quantization can reduce energy per operation on hardware that supports the lower-precision path, both by reducing bytes moved from DRAM and by reducing compute energy per MAC.
Because logic is 'free', minimizing FLOPs is the primary energy lever regardless of memory access patterns.
Since on-chip SRAM energy is orders of magnitude lower than DRAM, using more shared memory always reduces total energy without further conditions.

explanation: A: DRAM access dominates energy in DNN workloads; increasing on-chip reuse (weight stationary, output stationary etc.) is the primary energy optimization. B: Quantization reduces both DRAM traffic and per-MAC compute energy on hardware with matched low-precision paths (INT8, FP8 Tensor Cores). C is wrong because FLOP minimization ignores the dominant memory-energy term. D is wrong because SRAM helps only when it enables reuse; a larger on-chip buffer with poor reuse can still lose to DRAM if data is fetched fresh each time.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: memory access energy dominates; reuse and tiling are the primary levers.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: lower precision reduces bytes moved and compute energy per operation when hardware supports it.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: FLOP-only optimization misses the memory-energy dominance well documented in accelerator surveys.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: SRAM is only cheaper than DRAM per access; benefit requires reuse. Increasing SRAM without reuse is not a general energy win.

assumptions: Standard survey-scale relative energy figures (DRAM access ≫ SRAM access ≫ MAC).
Kernel-level accounting: energy per op includes both compute and data movement.
nonImplications: Does not imply that DRAM energy dominates in every kernel; small tensors that fit in cache may be compute-energy-dominated.
Does not imply that quantization always saves energy; if hardware lacks the low-precision datapath, dequantization overhead can erase gains.

distractorRationales.D: Misses the reuse condition for SRAM benefit.

sourceRefs.locator: Ch. 1-2, relative energy per operation and DNN accelerator design

performanceClaim.scope: DNN accelerator energy accounting, survey-scale relative costs
